### Performance
- **Streaming replies no longer re-render the whole transcript per token.** Text/thinking/tool-progress deltas now land in a dedicated per-tab stream store; the chat transcript (history turns, tool cards, input-area chrome, tray) stays untouched while the model streams. Deltas are also coalesced to once per animation frame instead of applying each provider chunk (40–150/s) directly.
- **Long replies stop getting slower as they grow.** The committed part of a streaming reply renders as independently memoized markdown blocks — each new delta re-parses only the newest block instead of re-running the full remark/rehype/KaTeX pipeline over the whole text every token (which was quadratic over a turn).
- **Turn-end freeze fixed for projects with many sessions.** The session store re-read and re-parsed every session JSON on each turn end (synchronously, on the main process, with pretty-printed writes). Reads are now served from an mtime-validated in-memory cache and writes are compact.
- New tabs prewarm the agent runtime in the background, so the first message skips permission-gate/tool-host/prompt-assembly/MCP startup and starts streaming much sooner. Prompt context assembly no longer re-scans the project from disk up to five times per first message (3 s TTL cache).
- Fixed a hidden cost where collapsed "Thinking" bodies kept re-running the full markdown pipeline on every streamed delta while invisible.

### Fixed
- **Figures in the final reply no longer disappear when the turn settles.** The hidden "Worked for" body used to keep rendering (and winning the one-visible-preview-per-figure claim) after the turn finished, so the same figure embedded in the reply rendered as nothing.
- **Streaming no longer makes activity folds jump open/closed.** Worked-for wrapping now happens exactly once, when the turn settles — not on every tool→prose→tool alternation mid-stream. Manual fold toggles always win over automatic open/close, and automatic collapsing no longer yanks scroll position. A rules-of-hooks violation in the streaming markdown renderer (intermittent content flicker / boundary crash) is fixed, as were duplicate React keys from the settled preamble/reply split.
- **Switching projects can no longer show the wrong file tree.** All async tree writers (metadata reload, watcher rescan, branch switch, content re-reads) now discard results if the focused project changed while they were in flight — a slow local scan can no longer overwrite the tree after you switch to a remote project, and vice versa. The same fix covers git status/branches, workspace config, literature, and experiments panels, which could previously paint one project's data over another.
- Project switches show a skeleton instead of the previous project's file tree while the new root is scanned, and file-watcher events from a previous project are ignored for the focused one.
- **Host terminals work on macOS.** The Host had no working PTY backend there — it silently fell back to plain pipes, where an interactive zsh never executes commands (it buffers until stdin closes) and races the Host for keystrokes, so terminal tabs sat dead or randomly lost input. A small system-perl helper now allocates a real PTY (grantpt **and** unlockpt ioctls — issuing only one leaves the slave locked), gives the shell a controlling tty with a real winsize, and relays master↔stdio; `terminal:create` waits for the relay handshake so the first keystroke cannot be lost.

### Remote
- **Remote file trees now update on their own.** The Host runs a lightweight change watcher and forwards `fs:fileChanged` events over the existing session channel (3 s snapshot diff, dot-directories skipped, ~50k files capped); the laptop routes `fs:watch-start`/`fs:watch-stop` to the Host instead of silently doing nothing. Remote trees and git status refresh themselves instead of waiting for a manual refresh.
- **A dropped SSH connection no longer flashes "Connect" screens.** While the Host auto-reconnects, panels keep their last-known content under a dismiss-free "reconnecting, content may be stale" banner — reconnecting is a self-healing state, not an error requiring action. Only a genuinely offline Host (never connected / errored) still shows the Connect prompt.
- **Returning to a project brings your tabs back.** The open RightArea tabs (files, terminals, Git overview, Library/Experiment/Interaction panels) are archived per project when you switch away and restored when you switch back — including the case where a lazy remote focus closed everything while the Host was still connecting. Terminal tabs restore with the same working directory (the shell process itself is fresh; long-running terminal jobs do not survive the switch).

### Developer
- Sessions persist as compact JSON (was pretty-printed) — the machine-runtime store shrinks on disk roughly 2–3×.
- `agent:prewarm` IPC for background runtime startup; `send()` verifies the prewarmed context (team roster / skills / MCP allowlist) and rebuilds on mismatch.
